title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a permitting and compliance failure at the infrastructure layer of a data center, not a failure of a model or of software. The generators were installed and run without the permits New Jersey requires for either step, which means the site was drawing on power equipment that had never been through the state's review. The failure sits upstream of any compute: the campus was being brought into service while part of its power supply was outside the conditions under which it was allowed to operate.

Catching it would not have required anything sophisticated. It would have required the operator to check its own equipment against state permit requirements before installation, or an internal compliance step that flagged 62 unpermitted units before inspectors reached the site in late July. Detection came from the state, not from the operator, and the penalty followed.

What the reporting does not establish is intent. Operating without a permit is a violation, not proof that the omission was deliberate, and the federal lawsuit over noise is an allegation that has not been adjudicated. The reports also do not establish what workloads the Vineland site hosts or who its tenants are.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators at its Vineland data center site in late July. The 2,000 kilowatt generators lacked required permits to be installed or operated. The penalty, issued Tuesday, is the largest ever for a data center operator in New Jersey and was for violating the state's Air Pollution Control Act.

The Vineland campus is planned as a 2.6 million square foot complex needing 350 megawatts of power, enough for a medium size city. Some of it is already in use. It is slated for completion at the end of the year. Homeowners have filed a federal lawsuit against DataOne over persistent noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department has issued violation orders for excessive noise.
